claims: There was a tie in the Best Live Action Short Film category at the 2026 Oscars with "The Singers" (Sam A. Davis and Jack Piatt) and "Two People Exchanging Saliva" (Alexandre Singh and Natalie Musteata) both winning.
The 2026 Oscars tie marked the seventh tie in Academy Awards history.
The 2026 Oscars tie was the first since 2013.
Kumail Nanjiani announced the tie, confirming it was not a joke, notes BuzzFeed and Variety.
"The Singers" and "Two People Exchanging Saliva" both received the award, states NBC News and People.com.
This was only the seventh tie in nearly 100 years of Oscar history.
Before 2026, the most recent tie was at the 2013 Oscars for Sound Editing (Skyfall and Zero Dark Thirty).
There was a tie in 1995 for Live Action Short Film (Trevor and Franz Kafka's It's a Wonderful Life), notes Vogue.
There was a tie in 1969 for Best Actress (Katharine Hepburn for The Lion in Winter and Barbra Streisand for Funny Girl).
There was a tie in 1932 for Best Actor (Wallace Beery and Fredric March).
